latin: Contingentia ad utrumlibet futurorum cognitorum a deo simul stat cum infallibilitate diuinae scientiae.

mentions.context: and probably cannot, reflect even some of the complexities involved in this issue, being a conclusion or a thesis only. The next two theses also deal with the problem of future contingencies and originate in the same place in Thomas’s Summa. Thesis 4 emphasizes that the contingent nature for us of each of the future contingencies, is from God’s per- spective, necessary, as a concomitant of the infallibility of divine knowledge;14 we have already seen these notions in Thomas (nn. 11–13). 13 Ibid.: “Unde manifestum est quod contingentia et infallibiliter a Deo cognoscuntur, inquantum subduntur divino conspectui secundum suam praesentialitatem: et tamen sunt futura contingentia, suis causis comparata.” 14 Pico, 900 Theses, p. 220: “Contingentia ad utrumlibet futurorum cognitorum a Deo simul stat cum infallibilitate divinae scientiae.” 15 Ibid.: “Quodcunque contingens Deus scivit esse futurum, necessario scivit illud esse futurum.”
